author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest traced that persistent feeling of not being enough back to Psalm 42, the image of a deer panting for streams of water, a longing Carl Jung himself referenced in his correspondence with the founder of Alcoholics Anonymous. He argued men are handed a specific image of what a man is supposed to look like, and that even the fiercest, most effective men, if you get them talking honestly, will admit to deep feelings of inadequacy and worthlessness underneath it all. Russell reflected that this deficiency exists because men are never told the actual solution, that real identity is found in God, and without that reconciliation, they end up chasing fulfillment using the culture's own tools and metrics instead, a system he argued isn't just ineffective, it's actually designed to keep people in constant want. Sometimes the problem was never the striving, it was what you were striving toward.

title: This is why success never feels like enough...

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell revisited an old clip of Jim Carrey and Jenny McCarthy on Larry King, back when the two were married and openly campaigning for caution around childhood vaccines, following what they believed may have been a vaccine injury to their own son. Jenny argued parents deserve to make educated decisions, space out vaccines, and question why doctors wouldn't want more information about something with real risks, pointing out that both the AAP and medical schools receive funding from drug companies. Russell followed it with a satirical bit imagining the industry's real response to Jim speaking out, tying his outspokenness directly to the survival of his own blockbuster career, a pointed joke about how financial interests can quietly pressure public figures into silence. Sometimes the sharpest commentary is the one dressed up as a joke.
